# STDO Skills delivery

Both initial dogfood skill packages are built and have actual-host evidence.
Codex uses one progressive `stdo-work` skill; Claude uses a five-skill bundle.
They implement the same shared requirements with different host designs.
Codex's finite nested handoff and the repaired Claude lifecycle have independent
actual readback. **Claude's mandatory Q05 handoff on its declared CLI path remains
open.** These are implemented candidates with bounded evidence, not a fully
qualified or accepted delivery.

Start with the [Codex guide](../../../build_tenants/codex/README.md) or
[Claude installation guide](../../../build_tenants/claude/INSTALL.md). Use a
specifically selected workspace-local installation. The package guides retain
construction-era proof statements; this report indexes the later evidence without
mutating those frozen packages.

## What was built and used

The Product pins the proper published immutable STDO 3.0.1 RC1 methodology at
manifest `60356364a412dbde8cffe68fe0eda4e2749b0162acce93495534eee13b223df8`.
The STDO manager verified that installed basis. Current a_c tooling was extended
with a separately identified native 3.0.1 profile and used for source acquisition,
observations, context assembly, exact preflight, real host dispatch, scoped
publication and evidence/return handling. Its 103 affected checks passed; actual
host evidence and source review remain separate from those checks. Native
`results.conjoin` is explicitly unsupported.

The current package identities are:

- Codex inventory: `337d274efde96147c8e9a2db3e3b25f7631731fc8486562c9022ad087833aa36`.
- Claude repair-2 inventory: `33472e5e2b9adf5ba616bd6980d7f84b3c10de168968727919de32378f045704`.

Root selected the common baseline for construction. A fresh source-first Claude
review found no actionable S0–S2 defect in its acquired common/tool/Codex static
population; its actual native return was captured and checked consumable. Claude
packaging defects F-C02–04 were repaired and independently read back. The later
LC-01 actor scope failure led to a focused instruction repair and a fresh affected
host invocation, preserving the common criteria.

## Finite task evidence

| Cases | Current supported evidence and remaining distinction |
|---|---|
| Q01, Q02, Q04: entry and small work | Both hosts have automatic/explicit skill-use witnesses and a negative unrelated-task control. Correct scoped greeting and proportionate work are observed. Codex automatic execution retains a prohibited failed read-only Git attempt; full-attempt scope is not passed. |
| Q03, Q06: basis and tool failure | Both preserve missing/altered/ambiguous basis and failed build evidence. Deliberately unsupported conjoin discovery is observed; this does not cover every unsupported method branch. |
| Q05: nested handoff and review | Codex's installed Executive consumed the actual Worker's result and source-first nonauthor same-family Reviewer's assessment, then returned ready-for-owner-review; independent actual readback supports this finite path. Claude Q05 remains open on its declared CLI path. The operator-assisted MCP attempt reached a Worker that failed login before tools or candidate work; no candidate review or acceptance followed. |
| Q07–Q10: continuation and recovery | Common retained-obligation, stale-review, uncertain-effect and exhaustion distinctions have finite witnesses. Codex's history report is directly assessable although that actor timed out without a closed return. Claude's stronger C oracle remains unestablished and two S4 report ambiguities remain. |
| Q11: release | Both preparation witnesses and separately authorized local deployments are supported. Claude's original deployment timed out after acknowledged writes and actual comparisons; one same-session read-only close returned final status with unchanged workspace bytes. Independent readback supports that reconciled path, without passing the timed-out invocation. These demo trials do not reopen the methodology's released status. |
| Q12: package lifecycle | Codex's selected update/invoke/removal path is supported. Original Claude invocation fails LC-01 despite correct greeting. The current repaired invocation and exact scoped removal have independent actual readback. The reported eight-file count differs from the actual seven-file receipt and stays S4; a truncated manager verification pipeline does not supply its missing exit status. |

[EVIDENCE-INDEX.json](EVIDENCE-INDEX.json) binds every row to exact captures,
assessments, readbacks and package cuts. The readable
[lifecycle index](qualification/lifecycle/CASE-INDEX.md) separates each attempt
and its later continuation. Observation, author assessment, independent review and
Root disposition stay distinct. Historical evidence is reused only for unaffected
claims; one host or package cut does not qualify another.

## Retained limitations and next decision

Original author timeouts, F-C01 scope effects and initial admission interpretation
remain recorded. The construction observation-scope setup error, old failed
returns, fixture/capture failures and unknown effects are preserved. Later
successful paths do not retroactively repair them. Original LC-01's fixed `/tmp`
writes/deletions remain a failed actor attempt; unknown prior content/loss stays
unknown. The unknown nested tool-description S3 remains open, distinct from
intentional native conjunction refusal.

The Claude deployment close preserved all workspace files and performed no repeat
deployment. Its earlier return code 143, incomplete EOFs, missing usage and unknown
detached-descendant/external effects remain. The resumed session's vendor list
cost can include earlier usage and is not added as a new invocation-only cost.

The [Claude transport boundary review](review/CLAUDE_Q05_TRANSPORT_AND_HOST_BOUNDARY.md)
traces the attempted MCP path to the frozen design's explicit exclusion. That
operator choice does not extend the package contract. The failed nested
authentication is supplemental integration evidence; it establishes neither the
supported CLI handoff nor a general skill defect. The actual source-first
expectation remains retained, with no completed candidate review. The parent
closed after capturing and checking the failed Worker return as nonconsumable;
greeting and sentinel stayed unchanged. Initial diagnostic exposure and a later
mistyped Context refusal remain recorded. Independent [failure readback](review/CLAUDE_Q05_FAILURE_HOLD_READBACK.md)
confirms that hold and retains an S4 metadata-precision issue: protected
home-variable metadata and credential-name presence are different fields. The
cause of login refusal remains unestablished. Operator preparation materially
assisted these handoffs; autonomous setup and whole-attempt clean scope are not
claimed.
No further authentication workaround or mixed-host successor is selected.

The next needed qualification is one separately selected handoff using Claude's
declared CLI/Bash/Read route after usable child authentication, or a separately
designed and selected composition. It must supply an actual Worker result,
source-first candidate assessment and Executive consumption before the delivery
decision. Common criteria remain unchanged. This evidence does not
establish statistical reliability, comparative efficiency, owner acceptance,
a STDO Skills release or global deployment. Exact Codex model/cost and total
delivery cost remain unknown where not reported. Vendor list-price reports are
observations, not billing or savings.

The method pin remains static. Source-matched methodology representation and
fresh-machine manager onboarding are separate work; neither makes the published
STDO 3.0.1 RC1 cut a non-final release.

# STDO Skills

Status: selected common construction basis under T-001; both tenant implementations exist.
[Delivery evidence](../.ai-workspace/work/T001/DELIVERY.md) states the supported
finite claims and remaining work; Product acceptance and release are separate.

## Product boundary

Product identity: `urn:stdo:product-definition:stdo-skills`.
Bounded context: `urn:stdo-skills:bounded-context:agent-method-application`.

The Product supplies skills for F_P agents applying an exactly selected STDO
methodology to software-development work. It connects recognizable user tasks
to the deciding source, appropriate context, supported tool operations and
observable returns. It owns requirements for this user-facing capability and
evidence that each tenant realizes it.

STDO owns the method. a_c and other declared Development Products own their tool
contracts and computational implementations. A skill preserves and applies those
contracts; it does not create another lifecycle, state store or source of
assessment, admission, acceptance or publication authority.

## Selected methodology

The complete static builder and initial supported methodology is
`stdo://releases/v3.0.1-rc.1/`, manifest
`60356364a412dbde8cffe68fe0eda4e2749b0162acce93495534eee13b223df8`.
Native commit: `fe4941f56a52ed3697a2b516d8d68948b0ea65d9`;
package: `specification_methodology/v3`.
The [Product Definition](../stdo_skills.json) owns the operative locator.
The mutable `3.0.1` discovery channel is not an adoption instruction.

The release remains static while this Product's requirements, designs and skills
are developed. A later method adoption requires an explicit compatibility
decision and affected qualification; an implementation defect does not authorize
editing the selected methodology.

## Users and capability

The user works in a governed workspace using Codex or Claude. Skills support:

- setup and exact Product/method selection;
- intake and re-entry at the changed requirement, design or realization owner;
- context acquisition and bounded frame construction;
- authorized direct work or Executive-directed delegation;
- source-first independent review where required;
- continuation, recovery, currentness and truthful status;
- release preparation and separately authorized release operations.

The shared requirements state outcomes and discriminators. They do not prescribe
skill count, names, prompt identity, invocation syntax or host-specific mechanism.
Each tenant owns its computational and execution binding, including instructions,
supporting references, tool integration, installation and tuning.

## Tool relationship

The current `stdo` manager verifies and resolves the exact installation. The
separately implemented native a_c 3.0.1 profile supplies the selected public
acquisition, context, preflight, dispatch, Writer and evidence/return operations.
Its [owning design](../../a_c/build_tenants/graphify/design/fd-support-stdo-3.0.1.md)
states the supported fragment; native `results.conjoin` remains unsupported.
The legacy RC9 profile and its provenance remain distinct. Each operation's
supported claim follows its exact contract and actual evidence, not a label or
blanket calculus-conformance claim.

Tool harmonisation remains owned by a_c. This Product may identify required
contracts, report defects and consume a supported increment; it does not fork
tool semantics into each tenant. A skill's direct use of host facilities must
be declared in its design, preserve the selected operation contract and be
qualified on that actual path. It cannot substitute for a required tool result.

F_D classification follows the selected calculus's totality and dependency
requirements. An F_D constructor gains no assessment or admission authority from
that classification; invoking an F_P actor does not make its semantic answer
deterministic. The deciding owners are in [SOURCE_OWNERS.md](SOURCE_OWNERS.md).

## Independent tenants and releases

`build_tenants/codex/` and `build_tenants/claude/` independently realize the common
WHAT. Evidence and supported-host claims are tenant-specific. Both use the same
task semantics and acceptance predicates, while host realization and tuning may
differ materially. Common machinery is reused where its contract fits; retained
variants need a concrete supported difference.

This Product is a peer at the monorepo root. It has its own lifecycle and release
identity and is not automatically a member of an existing STDO release cohort.
The present work constructs candidates and performs bounded qualification; it
does not publish a release or install skills into unrelated user environments.

## Construction authority

Jim owns Product scope, common meaning, acceptance and release. His recorded
[T-001 instruction](../.ai-workspace/tickets/active/T-001-skills-dogfood.md#owner-instruction)
selects this Product, its two tenants, static method and Executive-directed
construction. Root is the bounded Executive for that work and can select
requirements/design candidates for construction, allocate exact Writer effects,
evaluate returns, request supported repairs and retain residuals within that
outcome. It cannot silently broaden Product meaning or claim owner acceptance.

Root selected the common [frame basis](REFERENCE_FRAME_BASIS.md) for bounded
construction at the original common inventory, recorded in the
[construction decision](../.ai-workspace/work/T001/operator/DECISIONS.md).
Subsequent actual native preflight receipts bind their exact operation contracts;
they do not retrospectively admit initial drafting or erase failed attempts.
The owner's work authorization, contract admission and Product acceptance remain
distinct. T-001 preserves that initial interpretation and the later evidence.

## Acceptance boundary

Initial delivery requires a coherent common specification, both realized tenant
designs, usable host installation paths, supported tool bindings, and independent
assessment of the [finite scenario evidence](requirements/SCENARIOS.md).
Missing or failed mandatory evidence withholds the corresponding supported claim.
It cannot be hidden by a suite total or by the other tenant succeeding.

Repeated use may establish broader reliability and benefit. This first experiment
supports only the cases, hosts, settings, tool versions and outcomes actually
observed. Product acceptance and release remain owner decisions on that evidence.

# Project reference-frame basis

Identity: `urn:stdo-skills:frame-basis:initial:1`.
Status: selected for bounded construction by Root at common inventory
`a6d348b8385ea453ce29362fb9d74559304b1b91743b3c9ea31a83a9f02b5f2d`,
recorded in [operator/DECISIONS.md](../.ai-workspace/work/T001/operator/DECISIONS.md).
This status projection changes no frame criteria or original frozen source.
Product acceptance and release remain separate.

## Method, outcome and authority

The complete method is STDO v3.0.1-rc.1, manifest
`60356364a412dbde8cffe68fe0eda4e2749b0162acce93495534eee13b223df8`.
Read the exact installed REFERENCE_FRAME and ACTIVATION owners. This configuration
applies the Executive/Worker/Reviewer relations of EXECUTIVE_BASELINE §§6, 8–10,
12 and 16 to the owner's selected dogfood construction, while retaining the
sufficient direct Writer branch. It makes no claim of completed profile
qualification or automatic applicability of every available specialist frame.

The governed mutable source is this `stdo_skills/` Product. The outcome is two
usable skill tenants satisfying the common requirements and assessed on the
finite declared tasks. Jim owns Product acceptance and release. Root's bounded
construction decisions and exact user instruction are in [T-001](../.ai-workspace/tickets/active/T-001-skills-dogfood.md).
An actor label supplies no effect grant or admission. The initial construction
interpretation and subsequent admission obligation remain explicit there.

## Frames and coordinates

| Frame | Evaluation and material attention | Authority, evidence and return |
|---|---|---|
| Executive `skills.executive/1` | Exact Product outcome, dependency-ready frontier, current candidate identities, closed returns, tool compatibility and remaining claims | Select only authorized bounded actions; no mutation in this frame; consumes source-bound returns and records decisions through a granted Writer |
| Worker `skills.worker/1` | Exact requirement/design, affected producers/consumers, selected host/tool contracts, operation territory and proof predicates | Construct only within grant; self-review and return exact candidate, performed/unperformed evaluations, effects, residuals and invalidators to Executive |
| Reviewer `skills.reviewer/1` | Source-derived expected behavior, exact frozen candidate and actual-path evidence, exposure history and test semantics | Independent assessment, not repair or promotion; return findings, severity, evidence, affected claims and uncertainty to Executive |
| Direct Writer `skills.direct-writer/1` | One sufficient local outcome, existing basis and effect grant, current preimage and focused proof | No coordination or independent review added solely from task existence; admission and exact territory still required; return to declared consumer |

Each activation names frame/revision, exact evaluation/result algebra, subject and
basis, material invariants, authorities, evidence/tools, capability/context
envelope, exclusions, dependencies, consumer and stop/re-entry conditions, as
REFERENCE_FRAME §11 requires. File identities use content hashes or exact commits;
host/model settings and tool/profile versions are material coordinates. Results
use ACTIVATION's work/result refinements with named predicates, not an invented
local pass algebra.

No actor receives the entire repository merely because it is available. The
Executive selects the deciding frontier. Workers acquire the causal cone needed
for their own change; Reviewers acquire sources independently. Measured task
context, actor capability and remaining unknowns accompany each activation.

## Known evaluation inventory and coverage

| Evaluation | Source and dependency | Current disposition |
|---|---|---|
| E01 Exact static method and definition | Product selection; manager verification | Exact installed pin verified; common selection and stable Product owner binding recorded |
| E02 Common outcome and requirement adequacy | Intent, Product, SK-01..12 | Selected for construction; actual source-first Claude static review reports no actionable S0–S2 in its acquired scope |
| E03 Tool contract compatibility | SK-04; exact a_c and manager implementations | Native binding implemented and used; 103 affected checks pass; results.conjoin unsupported and retained S3 discovery limitation |
| E04 Codex realization binding | E02, E03; tenant design and host contract | Implemented; exact package and evidence indexed in DELIVERY.md |
| E05 Claude realization binding | E02, E03; tenant design and host contract | Implemented; exact package and evidence indexed in DELIVERY.md |
| E06 Actual host discovery and task behavior | E04/E05; Q01..12 and independent oracle | Finite actual-host evidence retained; Claude repair-2 lifecycle and Codex Q05 independently supported; mandatory Claude Q05 on declared CLI transport remains open |
| E07 Independent candidate assessment | Frozen source and E06 evidence | Actual cross-family static assessment plus nonauthor host/lifecycle readbacks; Claude transport-boundary and closed failure-capsule readbacks retained; no completed Claude candidate review |
| E08 Delivery disposition and residuals | Current results for E01..07 | Initial dogfood packages implemented with bounded evidence; full qualification withheld by Claude Q05 gap; Jim retains acceptance/release |

Material interface, configuration, lifecycle, authority, recovery, proof and
usability concerns are covered through these evaluations and their causal seams.
The exact deployed skill package, actual host invocation and tool response form
the ordinary proof path. Hosted-service availability, general optimal context
selection, statistical model reliability and quantified benefit remain explicit
residuals until separately tested. No generic frame family is declared satisfied
merely because this table names a nearby concern.

## Conjunction, invalidation and decisions

For a claimed capability, all applicable required predicates must have current
support on compatible subjects/bases. Unknown applicability remains unresolved;
contradictory results require disposition, not majority voting. No implicit
translation joins different method or host coordinates. Root may retain valid
unaffected evidence and activates only the affected new evaluation after change.

Invalidate affected reliance after source/tool/profile/host change, changed
authority or scope, a counterexample, failed custody, or a context projection
that loses a required future distinction. An uncertain effect is reconciled
before retry. Failed construction re-enters the governing owner actually shown
to be insufficient; it does not automatically reopen all upstream design.

Review severity is S0 catastrophic irreversible harm or systemic unauthorized
effects; S1 major authority/basis violation or broadly unusable core outcome;
S2 reproducible material functional/semantic failure in a supported ordinary
path; S3 bounded defect with a practical workaround or limited consequence;
S4 minor clarity/usability issue without demonstrated material outcome failure.
The reviewer supplies the effect and evidence supporting that grade. Root assigns
work priority and decides the effect on the selected delivery claim separately.
A failed mandatory predicate or unresolved authority/effect condition withholds
its dependent claim regardless of severity; unrelated observations do not block
it. An initial common candidate or a successful test is not owner acceptance.

A nonauthor native subagent in the same model family supplies nonauthor evidence
with a semantic-independence limitation. It does not establish cross-family
independence. The frozen common/tool/Codex candidate received an actual fresh Claude review;
its exposure, selected population and actual resolved model remain in the
[retained return](../.ai-workspace/work/T001/operator/protected-evidence/objects/b56b4ebdb38d47bd27d35637fd16e79b1120a18e78322b27bcfde397b248b19a.json).
Later host readbacks and localized Codex-authored Claude repairs retain their own
independence limits and do not expand that review's claim.

Durable activation, result, decision and residual records live under T-001's work
surface. A fresh actor can reconstruct the frontier from those records and exact
source; chat memory and hidden reasoning are not required evidence.

branch `codex/stdo-skills`, initial repository base
`a2e56d8bd2882068c84e45b2423cecc246c62525`.

territory under the recorded owner instruction. Root explicitly directs the
initial Writer to consume that existing human authorization and create a
reviewable common candidate, without claiming a deterministic admission result.

human override of a later unseen contract, a tool-issued admission, an accepted
Project frame basis or proof of completed STDO application.

ACTIVATION §1 Admission requires exact-contract admission evidence for governed
execution. At initial drafting, integration with subsequent real delegated operation
contracts was open as E03. The later native binding and exact preflight receipts
now provide the selected operation path; they retrospectively admit nothing.
Each later execution retains its own observed admission, result and limitations. Recording a drafted

about the initial construction interpretation remains attached to these effects;

Deliver independently designed and usable Codex/Claude skill packages against
common requirements, static methodology and actual supported tools. Root is the
Executive: it keeps the outcome/frontier, selects bounded requirements/design

## Re-entry and stop conditions

Re-enter the relevant owner for missing or changed Product meaning, unsupported
tool semantics, insufficient context, actual host capability mismatch, invalid
source custody, or a counterexample to required behavior. Reconcile uncertain
effects before retry. Retain open obligations and prior attempts. Stop the
dependent operation for missing authority, an unresolved hard boundary, exhausted
declared envelope or an unsupported contract. Continue unrelated authorized work
where its basis remains sufficient.

adoption, Product scope change or publication returns to Jim with its concrete
consequences. Routine implementation choices and supported repairs stay within
